content.text: {"vat": "A bricklayer working on a timber scaffold (the image shows no uniform, headgear, insignia or weapon)", "dac_diem": "A man bends over a plank platform laying bricks. He wears a dark grey sleeveless waistcoat over a light grey long-sleeved shirt, grey trousers and a small dark cap. The scaffold is made of round poles lashed together, with wooden planks across them. A red brick wall is at the lower right, and part of another person's head and hat shows at the bottom.", "co_tu_nam": null, "da_co_nam_1667": "yes", "ly_do": "Pole-and-plank scaffolding and brick building were standard in London in 1667, especially during the rebuilding after the 1666 Great Fire. The waistcoat, shirt and cap are plain workman's clothes that fit the period. The image is too blurry to check the exact cut of the clothes."}
